• **Ohm’s Law**

 
 
• **Ohm’s law states that if the physical state (i.e. length, temperature, mechanical strain, material) of the conductor remains the same then the voltage applied across its ends is directly proportional to the current flowing through it.**
 
• **V ∝ I**
 
• **V = I R (V = Voltage, I = current, R = resistance)** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9a15752dc1dae4eb50d47e107525b336d12f65ff6488827427e8a34096ddf4d1.png] 
 
• This graph between V and I of a conductor at constant temperature shows that the gradient of change in the voltage (Δ V) is proportional to the change in current (Δ I).
 
• This makes the graph a straight line.
 
• R=VI
 
• The SI Unit of electrical resistance is “ohm (Ω)” or volt/amp
 
• The resistance of the conductor depends on the following factors:
 
• Length (l): The resistance of the conductor directly proportional to its length R ∝ l.
 
• Area of cross-section (A): Resistance is inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area of the conductor R ∝ 1/A
 
• The resistance of the conductor also depends on the nature of the material and temperature.
